title: Polynomial-Time Computability of Final Counts
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean words, let $i$ be one of its movement-count coordinates, and let $y$ map Boolean words to Boolean words and $T$ map Boolean words to natural numbers. If $y$ is polynomial-time computable and the function mapping $x$ to a unary word of length $T(x)$ is polynomial-time computable, then the function mapping $x$ to the binary representation of the movement count at coordinate $i$, after $T(x)$ steps of the count process for $M$ initialized on $y(x)$, is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine $M$ over Boolean words
A coordinate $i$ among the $\mathrm{clRecFields}(M)$ movement-count coordinates
A polynomial-time computable function $y$ from Boolean words to Boolean words
A function $T$ from Boolean words to natural numbers whose unary length word is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If a reference-input producer and a unary-horizon producer are polynomial-time computable, then for every counter coordinate the function sending an input to the binary representation of that movement count at the produced horizon is polynomial-time computable; keeping the time unary avoids any exponential clock.
